item.text: I’m using the flexsds-advisor skill to inspect the local hardware and serving checks, then produce a preview without starting a server.

item.aggregated_output:
---
name: flexsds-advisor
description: Inspect FlexSDS hardware/profile selection, check target/draft serving setup, construct safe FlexSDS commands, and diagnose FlexSDS CLI errors from model IDs, environment facts or command output. Return observed results, caveats and exact next actions. Use for FlexSDS setup/advisory requests; exclude generic Python, vLLM scheduling, speculative-decoding theory and unrelated GPU advice.
---

# FlexSDS Advisor

Use the actual CLI for execution; keep reasoning and recommendations here. Support
hardware/profile inspection, serving configuration previews and CLI diagnosis.

1. Identify inspection, command construction, diagnosis, or explicitly requested
   real serving/stop action. For invocation details or unexpected output, read
   [the CLI contract](references/flexsds-cli.md). For performance, tree, support or
   optimality questions, read [claim boundaries](references/claim-boundaries.md).
2. Locate `flexsds`; inspect `--version` and `--help` when the installed contract is
   unknown. In a known source checkout, `python -m flexsds.cli.main` with that
   checkout's `src` on PYTHONPATH is the same entrypoint. If neither works, report
   the exact missing executable/import and suggest installation into the user's
   chosen environment; do not install or change credentials automatically.
3. For hardware use `flexsds detect`; for profile lookup use `flexsds profile`.
   CPU fallback means CUDA was not detected by this Python environment, not proof
   that no physical GPU exists. CPU memory is RAM, never serving VRAM. Unknown SM
   and CPU select the L4 profile; that is not measured support for this machine.
4. For configuration obtain both nonempty target and draft IDs plus backend.
   Ask for missing inputs. Reject option-like IDs and control characters; pass
   IDs as individual argv values with shell-appropriate quoting, never shell
   interpolation. Validate port 1–65535 if supplied. Do not replace user models.
   For advice with unspecified backend, explicitly label a local preview as such:

   ```text
   flexsds serve --target TARGET_ID --draft DRAFT_ID --backend local --dry-run
   ```

   Always include both IDs: bare `flexsds` or incomplete `serve`, even with
   `--dry-run`, enters the interactive wizard. Never automate that wizard.
   Capture command, exit code, stdout/stderr with a bounded timeout and closed
   stdin. Inspect warning/error text even on exit 0; do not treat it as readiness.
   Unsafe previews print "Launch blocked" and return 0; real unsafe serving
   returns 2 before dispatch. Compatibility is heuristic, not proof of model fit.
   Modal uses an estimated remote GPU budget, not local free memory.
5. Default to inspection/explanation/dry-run. A question such as "can this run?"
   does not authorize a launch. Real `serve`, background start, `stop`, paid GPU
   allocation, deployment and credential changes require explicit user intent.
   Existing explicit intent suffices; do not ask again for routine steps. Before
   an authorized action, inspect backend prerequisites and dry-run the exact
   configuration. Stop at missing GPU/runtime, OOM warnings, unsupported hardware
   or an option the runner cannot honor. Report the narrow blocker and next fix;
   never substitute cloud or broaden the action. Read backend limitations in
   the reference before launch. Colab flag mode provides guidance only.
   `--no-adaptive` retains static speculation with the default vLLM scheduler.
   Local serving binds 0.0.0.0; verify that exposure matches the user's intent.
   For stop verify CWD, PID ownership and platform support first; do not stop an
   unrelated process or infer that local stop terminates Modal. Never collect
   secrets in chat. Check credential presence only, without printing values.
6. For `auth`, `chat` or `monitor`, read the CLI reference first. Login/logout
   changes credentials; never put secrets in argv or chat. Chat performs network
   inference; its displayed rates count SSE chunks, not tokens. Monitor tails a
   local trace until interrupted; bound observation and do not imply endpoint health.
7. On unavailable CLI, nonzero exit, timeout, or printed runner error, preserve
   the failure and explain a specific repair. Do not retry as a real launch or
   silently drop flags. Use supplied command/error text for diagnosis; reproduce
   only safe inspection/preview commands. Actual parser/runtime wins over docs;
   do not invent `test`, `check-compat`, `--json` or unsupported options.
8. Return the result, issue/limitation and exact next action. Label evidence as
   FACT (code contract), OBSERVATION (captured output), INFERENCE, RECOMMENDATION
   or UNKNOWN where relevant. A printed command is not a running endpoint.
   Never promise TreeAdaptive runtime, profitability, optimal hardware policy,
   no slowdown or adaptive speedup without matching controlled runtime evidence.

# Current CLI contract

Reconciled 2026-11-13 against backend 76957514f9a52e11d9a0a2322469d1a45cba9273
plus the Skill integration changes. Actual parser/source wins over documentation.
Version remains 0.2.0-alpha: record execution Git SHA too. No JSON output contract.

| Command | Arguments / behavior | Effects and exits |
|---|---|---|
| --help, --version | Parser exits before detection | Read-only, 0; parser errors 2 |
| detect | Torch detection, exceptions fall back to CPU/RAM | Inspection, 0; RAM is not VRAM |
| profile | sm_89 -> L4; sm_75 -> T4; other -> L4; missing file -> analytical_fallback | Lookup, not calibration or validated hardware support |
| auth status | Masked stored credentials | Reads ~/.flexsds/credentials; no provider validation or environment-only token report |
| auth login | --provider {modal,huggingface,cloudflare}, --key; getpass prompt | Writes credentials; never recommend --token with a secret in argv |
| auth logout | Optional --provider, otherwise all stored providers | Deletes stored keys and matching process environment; explicit intent |
| Complete serve --dry-run | Shared preflight plus generated command | Preview 0 even when blocked; no process, weights, credential access or port probe |
| Real local serve | Preflight, port probe, vLLM subprocess | Unsafe 2 before runner; runner None -> 1; foreground waits and propagates status |
| Real Modal serve | Shared remote budget, credentials, standalone HTTP app | modal serve (ephemeral) or modal deploy; subprocess status propagated; cloud effects |
| serve --backend colab | Repository notebook guidance | 0 means guidance; no endpoint or model forwarding |
| chat | --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1, --model, --temperature 0 | Health HTTP then interactive SSE inference POSTs; initially unreachable 1; normal exit 0 |
| monitor | --trace-file telemetry/serving_trace.jsonl, --refresh-rate 1 (positive) | Tails file, waits if absent, skips malformed JSON; Ctrl+C 0; not endpoint health |
| stop | CWD .flexsds.pid, local only | POSIX process-group SIGTERM and PID removal; verify ownership. Windows unsupported |
| Bare/incomplete serve | Interactive wizard, even incomplete --dry-run | Never automate: config writes/launch possible; unsafe guard -> CLI 2 before writing/launching |

Serve flags: --target, --draft, --backend {modal,local,colab} (default modal),
--gpu {L4,T4,A10G} (default L4; remote budget/Modal allocation), --port (1..65535,
default 8000), --background, --deploy, --no-adaptive, --dry-run.
Pass both exact nonempty model IDs, explicitly select backend, use argv arrays.
Printed joined commands are not shell-escaped.

## Guard and readiness

Flag mode and wizard consume evaluate_serving_preflight(), which combines
check_compatibility() and pre_download_guard(). It supplies mock_metadata={} for
offline name/dtype estimates, so no metadata HTTP or weights are fetched.
Both results must be safe. OOM, incompatible report, unsafe pre-download result,
or missing local CUDA blocks real dispatch. Known Qwen/Llama cross-family pairs
are rejected. This is heuristic validation, not tokenizer/kernel support.

Threshold: estimates must fit 95% of budget. Local budget is detected free VRAM;
remote budgets are L4 23000 MB, T4 15000 MB, A10G 22000 MB. Those are conservative
assumptions, not measured container memory. Laptop RAM/VRAM does not decide remote
GPU compatibility. Unsafe dry-run prints "Launch blocked", shows the preview and
returns 0. Unsafe real serving returns 2 with no runner call. Launch failure
returns 1; foreground child exits propagate. Started process/background PID/
successful deployment is not endpoint readiness or performance evidence.
ADAPTIVE_ENABLE_VRAM_GUARD controls runtime speculative budgets separately.

## Backend details

Local binds 0.0.0.0. Runner/wizard defaults are Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ and
duckhoi/qwen2.5-7b-eagle3.1-speculator. Never substitute these for user inputs.
Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct selects draft_model, not eagle3. Adaptive commands add
AdaptiveAsyncScheduler, LineageUniProcExecutor and per-request metrics.
--no-adaptive keeps static speculation and omits the custom scheduler/executor
and dynamic batch lookup; it does not make a vanilla baseline.
Port conflict stops Popen, but probing is not atomic reservation.
Background/stop are POSIX-only. Never stop an unrelated/stale PID.

Modal forwards exact non-secret model/draft/method/port/GPU/adaptive settings in
FLEXSDS_SERVING_CONFIG via an allowlist; modal_app declares GPU resources and
web_server port and reuses the local command builder. Dry-run never accesses
credentials. Real launch accepts environment/stored Modal ID+secret or existence
of ~/.modal.toml; presence is not verified authentication. Configure both keys
securely: default auth login saves only the ID. modal serve exposes a temporary
public development URL; deploy persists. Live cloud serving is not established
by mocked tests. Official references:
https://modal.com/docs/guide/webhooks
https://modal.com/docs/reference/modal.web_server

Colab flag mode gives guidance only. Wizard can show instructions and probe a
supplied tunnel URL. The notebook is a fixed EAGLE example with installation and
tunnel effects; configure exact models on that machine. Its develop URL is not
available until the notebook is published there. No local command opens a
notebook, creates a tunnel or launches a Colab server.

vLLM, CUDA, quantization kernels and repository src.server/src.proposer imports
are separate prerequisites. pyproject installs only psutil; a lightweight
installation does not establish the full serving runtime.

## Client, credentials and platform limits

Chat uses /models then root /health and POST /chat/completions. Chunk count/rate
and ms/chunk measure SSE content chunks, not tokenizer tokens, token throughput,
TPOT or speedup. Streaming has no explicit read timeout.
Monitor does not repair partial-line loss or file rotation.

Credentials are JSON outside the repo; POSIX 0700/0600 modes are attempted.
Windows ACL confidentiality is not established by chmod/stat. Never claim
universal zero-leak security or place tokens in URLs, argv, logs or chat.
Imported helper artifacts now use public Git URLs; historical removal is not
revocation: CREDENTIAL ROTATION STILL REQUIRED BY OWNER.

Windows output preserves Unicode when supported with ASCII fallback for cp1252/
unknown streams, including auth/chat/monitor/TaskRunner/Modal. No global stream
reconfiguration required.

Unsupported doc examples: test --endpoint, check-compat, detect --json,
--adaptive, serve --gpu-memory-utilization, profile calibration.
Plan checkboxes and historical worklogs are not current runtime proof.
# Claim boundaries

- FACT: canonical v0.2 serving is linear adaptive speculative decoding. A class,
  banner, help text or UI labelled TreeAdaptive is not tree runtime evidence.
  TreeAdaptive runtime and arbitrary external tree execution remain future work.
- OBSERVATION: report detected hardware, selected profile, warning text and printed
  command with version/environment/exit code. A CPU fallback may hide a Torch or
  driver failure. Profile selection is lookup, not calibration or optimality.
- INFERENCE: compatibility is a name/VRAM heuristic. It neither validates weights,
  tokenizer alignment, quantization kernels nor proves memory fit. L4 fallback on
  other hardware cannot support measured hardware-aware policy claims.
- RECOMMENDATION: suggest a dry-run or a controlled benchmark; keep model changes
  explicit and explain assumptions. Do not invent alpha, acceptance, latency or
  percentage speedups. Analytical cost-model outputs are predictions, not measurements.
- UNKNOWN: adaptive-vs-vanilla speedup, profitability and no-slowdown behavior
  without controlled comparable measurements of the exact workload/configuration.
  Historical M4-02-04 evidence (including 49/49 acceptance) is configuration-specific
  and cannot generalize. Matching hardware alone is insufficient.
- IMPLEMENTED WITH LIMITATION: chat streams HTTP/SSE and monitor reads JSONL.
  Chunk-rate metrics are not token throughput or TPOT. Preflight blocks unsafe
  launch estimates; it does not prove model fit or cloud endpoint readiness.
- Deferred: performance diagnosis, refactoring external OpenAI clients, optimal
  policy selection, distributed serving, external publication and cross-agent
  support. No real cloud deployment is verified by this skill's local tests.

Do not repeat README/product guarantees as established results. A successful
preview does not prove launch, readiness, endpoint compatibility or performance.
